name: Arkansas
headline_status: Medical cannabis is legal for registered patients; recreational use remains illegal.
summary: Arkansas voters approved a medical cannabis constitutional amendment in 2016, and dispensary sales began in Hot Springs in May 2019; the program now serves more than 115,000 patients. Voters rejected adult-use legalization in 2022, and the state Supreme Court blocked the count on a 2024 medical expansion measure. Possessing up to four ounces without a card is a misdemeanor that can bring jail time. A 2023 law (Act 629) banning intoxicating hemp products such as delta-8 became enforceable after a federal appeals court ruling in June 2025.

medical_since.value: Voters approved the medical cannabis amendment in 2016; first dispensary sales took place in May 2019.

retail_sales.value: Medical-only. The first sales were at Doctors Orders Rx in Hot Springs in May 2019. No adult-use stores exist.

medical_program.value: Patients with a physician certification apply online to the Department of Health for a registry card ($50 application or renewal). Visiting patients can get a 90-day card for $50. More than 115,000 patients are enrolled.

regulator.value: Arkansas Department of Health issues patient cards; the Medical Marijuana Commission and Alcoholic Beverage Control oversee and license cultivators and dispensaries.

penalties.value: Possessing up to four ounces without legal protection is a Class A misdemeanor carrying up to one year in jail and a fine up to $2,500, plus an automatic six-month driver's license suspension on conviction.

hemp_thc.value: Act 629 of 2023 bans psychoactive hemp products such as delta-8 and delta-9 THC; the Eighth Circuit lifted an injunction against it on June 24, 2025, allowing enforcement.

ballot_history.value: Adult-use legalization (Issue 4) failed in 2022, 56.3% to 43.7%. In October 2024 the state Supreme Court ruled votes on a medical expansion measure would not be counted.

timeline.event: Voters approve the medical cannabis constitutional amendment
First medical cannabis sales at Doctors Orders Rx in Hot Springs
Act 629 bans psychoactive hemp products; enforcement is initially blocked in court
Arkansas Supreme Court rules votes on a medical expansion initiative will not be counted
Gov. Sanders vetoes HB 1889, which would have allowed drive-through dispensary service
Eighth Circuit lets Arkansas enforce its ban on intoxicating hemp products

faq.a: Only for registered medical patients. Recreational use is illegal, and voters rejected an adult-use amendment in 2022.

faq.q: How do you get a medical marijuana card in Arkansas?
faq.a: Get a certification from a physician for a qualifying condition, then apply online to the Arkansas Department of Health. The application fee is $50.

faq.q: What is the penalty for marijuana possession in Arkansas?
faq.a: Possessing up to four ounces is a Class A misdemeanor punishable by up to a year in jail and a $2,500 fine, and a conviction triggers a six-month license suspension.
No. Act 629 of 2023 bans psychoactive hemp products such as delta-8, and a federal appeals court allowed the state to enforce it in June 2025.

faq.q: Can out-of-state patients buy medical cannabis in Arkansas?
faq.a: Yes. Visiting patients can apply online for a 90-day visiting patient card for $50.
